figures.anchorInterpretation: The fixed fee and hourly rate have different parameter meanings.
figures.mechanism: Define every quantity and unit, identify the direction of dependency, and check that terms combined in a formula have compatible units.
figures.validStructure: The same symbol can play different roles in different models; the context determines whether it is input, output, or parameter.

figures.lessonOutcome: Identify the input, output, parameters, and units in a quantitative relationship and explain how the quantities depend on one another.

figures.title: Mapping comparison

figures.mechanism: Check repeated inputs in a table, outgoing arrows in a mapping, vertical intersections in a graph, or the rule stated by a context.

figures.lessonOutcome: Determine whether a relation is a function by applying the rule that each allowed input has exactly one output.

figures.anchorProblem: Find domain of ln(x-1)/sqrt(x+2).
figures.anchorInterpretation: The logarithm and denominator-root conditions are intersected.
figures.mechanism: Write each restriction separately, solve it, intersect the solution sets, and retain exclusions hidden by cancellation.
figures.validStructure: A square root in a denominator requires a strictly positive radicand, while an ordinary square root allows zero.
figures.invalidMove: A frequent error is checking only one restriction or using the simplified formula's larger domain.
figures.lessonOutcome: Determine the real domain of a function by combining denominator, even-root, logarithm, and composition restrictions.

figures.mechanism: Begin with the algebraic domain, then apply nonnegativity, capacity, integer, safety, time-window, and evidence-range restrictions.

figures.invalidMove: A frequent error is reporting all real numbers for a model involving time, length, population, or counts.
figures.lessonOutcome: Distinguish the algebraic domain of a formula from the inputs that are meaningful in a model.

figures.anchorInterpretation: The secant rises 15 over a run of 3.
figures.mechanism: Evaluate both endpoints, subtract in matching order, simplify, attach compound units, and interpret the sign over the interval.

figures.lessonOutcome: Calculate and interpret average rate of change as output change per input change and as the slope of a secant line.
